name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on bench, feet on floor
Grip bar just wider than shoulder-width
Unrack, lower to mid-chest with control
Press back up explosively to lockout
Re-rack with control
tips: Keep shoulder blades pinched and retracted
Drive feet into floor for stability
Bar should touch lower chest, not neck

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat, hold dumbbells at chest level
Press up until arms are nearly fully extended
Lower with control, feeling stretch in chest
Keep wrists stacked over elbows throughout
tips: Greater range of motion than barbell
Allow slight natural arch in lower back
Neutral or pronated grip both work

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
instructions: Lie flat, hold dumbbells above chest, slight elbow bend
Lower dumbbells in wide arc until you feel chest stretch
Squeeze chest to bring dumbbells back together
Maintain slight bend in elbows throughout
tips: Think 'hugging a tree', not pressing
Don't go below shoulder level
Control the eccentric — most growth happens here

name: Pec Deck Machine
instructions: Sit with back flat against pad
Grip handles or place forearms on pads
Squeeze arms together in front of chest
Hold contraction briefly, then slowly release
tips: Keep elbows at shoulder height throughout
Excellent chest isolation for beginners
Don't let the weight slam back — control the negative

name: Push Up
instructions: Start in high plank, hands slightly wider than shoulders
Lower chest toward floor, elbows at 45 degrees
Stop just before chest touches
Push back up to full arm extension
tips: Keep core braced and body in straight line
Full range of motion beats half reps
Elevate feet to increase difficulty

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Mount parallel bars, arms straight
Lean torso forward at roughly 30 degrees
Lower until shoulders are below elbows
Press back to starting position
tips: Lean forward to emphasize chest over triceps
Keep elbows flared slightly outward
Use a dip belt for added resistance

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Adjust seat so handles are at chest height
Grip handles, elbows slightly below shoulder height
Press forward to full extension
Control return to start
tips: Good for beginners learning pressing pattern
Safer than free weights for solo training
Adjust seat height to match your chest

name: Conventional Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot
Hinge at hips, grip bar just outside legs
Chest up, lats engaged, take slack out of bar
Push floor away — drive hips forward as bar passes knees
Stand tall at top, lower with control
tips: Keep bar close to shins throughout lift
Think 'leg press the floor' not 'pull'
Big breath and brace core before every rep

name: Barbell Row
instructions: Hip-width stance, hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees
Grip bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder-width
Pull bar to lower abdomen, leading with elbows
Squeeze shoulder blades at top
Lower with control
tips: Keep lower back neutral throughout
Don't use momentum — control both phases
Elbow path determines which muscles fire most

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with thighs under pads, grip bar wider than shoulders
Lean back slightly, initiate with shoulder blades
Pull bar to upper chest
Slowly extend arms back to start
tips: Initiate with elbows driving down, not biceps curling
Slight lean back is okay — excessive is cheating
Full extension at top for maximum stretch

name: Pull Up
instructions: Hang from bar with overhand grip wider than shoulders
Depress and retract shoulder blades to initiate
Pull until chin clears the bar
Lower with full control to dead hang
tips: Dead hang start forces full range of motion
Think elbows to back pockets
Add weight via dip belt when bodyweight is easy

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Hang from bar with underhand grip shoulder-width
Pull chest toward bar, elbows driving to sides
Top position: chin over bar
Lower all the way to dead hang
tips: Underhand grip activates biceps more than pull-up
Supinate wrists at top for peak bicep contraction
Easier than pull-up for most beginners

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Place one knee and hand on bench for support
Hold dumbbell in free hand, arm extended
Pull dumbbell to hip, elbow driving toward ceiling
Lower with control to full extension
tips: Elbow stays close to body — don't flare out
Think 'elbow to ceiling' not 'hand to hip'
Full stretch at bottom is key for lat activation

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set cable at forehead height with rope attachment
Grab rope with palms facing in, step back
Pull rope toward face, elbows high and flared
Externally rotate wrists at end — 'W' position
Slowly return to start
tips: Essential for shoulder health and rear delt development
Elbows must stay above wrist height
Use light weight and high reps

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Set cable at high position, grab straight bar
Stand back, arms extended at chest height
Keeping arms straight, push bar down to hips
Squeeze lats at bottom, slowly return
tips: Excellent lat isolation without biceps involvement
Slight bend in elbows is fine
Focus on the feeling in your lats — mind-muscle connection

name: Rack Pull
instructions: Set pins in rack at knee height
Grip bar, set back flat with chest up
Drive hips forward, stand tall
Lower bar back to pins with control
tips: Allows heavier loading than full deadlift
Focuses on upper portion of deadlift
Keep lats tight to prevent bar drifting forward

name: Good Morning
instructions: Bar on upper traps, feet shoulder-width
Slight bend in knees, hinge forward at hips
Lower torso toward parallel with floor
Drive hips forward to return to upright
tips: Keep spine neutral — not rounded
Feel stretch in hamstrings at bottom
Use light weight and focus on movement pattern

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Lie perpendicular on bench, upper back supported
Hold dumbbell vertically above chest
Lower dumbbell in arc behind head
Pull back over chest with lat engagement
tips: Feel the stretch in lats and serratus
Keep slight bend in elbows throughout
Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up

name: Reverse Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Hinge forward 45-90 degrees, dumbbells hanging
With slight elbow bend, raise arms out to sides
Squeeze rear delts and rhomboids at top
Lower with control
tips: Lead with elbows, not hands
Pinch shoulder blades at peak
Use lighter weight — rear delts are small

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set barbell at hip height in rack
Lie underneath, grip overhand, body straight
Pull chest to bar, elbows back
Lower to arm extension with body rigid
tips: Easier than pull-ups, great progression
Elevate feet to increase difficulty
Keep body rigid like a plank throughout

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with thighs under pads, grip bar wide
Lean slightly back, depress shoulder blades
Pull bar to upper chest
Slowly extend back to full stretch
tips: Wide grip emphasizes lat width
Don't pull behind neck — bad for shoulder health
Full stretch at top is crucial

name: Barbell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with bar at collarbone, hands just outside shoulders
Brace core, glutes tight
Press bar overhead to lockout
Bar should travel slightly back over ears at top
Lower to collarbone with control
tips: Keep wrists straight — don't let them roll back
Elbows slightly forward at start, not flared
Press your head through at lockout

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit or stand, dumbbells at ear level, palms forward
Press dumbbells up and slightly together
Lockout overhead without shrugging
Lower to ear level with control
tips: Seated provides more stability, standing engages core more
Don't crash the weights at bottom
Slight arc inward at top — natural movement

name: Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides
With slight elbow bend, raise arms out to sides
Stop at shoulder height — slight tilt so pinkies slightly higher
Lower slowly — this is where the work is
tips: Lead with elbows, not wrists
Pause briefly at top
Slow negatives (3-4s) maximize stimulus

name: Front Raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells in front of thighs
Raise one or both arms to shoulder height
Slight bend in elbows throughout
Lower with control
tips: Targets anterior (front) delt
Can alternate arms or do both simultaneously
Keep core tight — don't lean back

name: Arnold Press
instructions: Start with dumbbells at chin, palms facing you
As you press up, rotate palms to face forward
Reach full lockout overhead
Reverse rotation on the way down
tips: Hits all three delt heads through rotation
Invented by Arnold Schwarzenegger
Use lighter weight than standard press initially

name: Upright Row
instructions: Stand holding bar with narrow overhand grip
Pull bar straight up to chin level
Elbows lead and stay above wrists
Lower with control
tips: Wider grip reduces impingement risk
Stop at collarbone level if you feel shoulder discomfort
Can also use dumbbells or EZ bar

name: Rear Delt Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Sit at edge of bench, hinge forward onto thighs
Dumbbells hanging with slight elbow bend
Raise arms out to sides at shoulder height
Squeeze rear delts, lower with control
tips: Can also do standing or prone on incline bench
Use lighter weights — rear delts are small
Think 'showing your armpits' to get the motion right

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at sides
Shrug shoulders straight up toward ears
Hold at top for 1-2 seconds
Lower slowly back down
tips: Don't roll shoulders — straight up and down
Pause at top to eliminate momentum
Traps respond well to heavy loads and high volume

name: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Hold barbell in front of thighs with overhand grip
Shrug shoulders directly upward
Pause and squeeze at top
Lower with control
tips: Allows heavier loading than dumbbells
Straps help maintain grip with heavy weights
Full range of motion beats heavy partial reps

name: Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust seat so handles are at ear level
Grip handles, back flat against pad
Press to full overhead extension
Lower with control
tips: Safer than free weights overhead
Great for beginners building shoulder strength
Back support allows heavier loading

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand holding bar with underhand grip, shoulder-width
Keep elbows tucked at sides
Curl bar to shoulder level
Slowly lower to full extension
tips: Don't swing — keep elbows pinned to torso
Supinate wrists slightly at top for peak contraction
Full extension at bottom maximizes stretch

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, palms forward
Curl one or both dumbbells to shoulder level
Squeeze bicep at top
Lower to full extension
tips: Allows each arm to work independently
Supinate from neutral grip during the curl for extra activation
Alternate arms or do both simultaneously

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, thumbs facing up (neutral grip)
Curl dumbbells to shoulder level, maintaining neutral grip
Squeeze at top
Lower with control
tips: Works brachialis — fills out the arm more
Can do cross-body hammer curls for variation
Heavier than supinated curls for most lifters

name: Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on bench, lean forward, brace elbow on inner thigh
Hang dumbbell toward floor
Curl to shoulder level
Squeeze hard at top, lower slowly
tips: Braced elbow eliminates cheating
Great for isolating individual arms
Mind-muscle connection is key here

name: EZ Bar Curl
instructions: Hold EZ bar at angled grips, stand upright
Curl bar to shoulder level, elbows fixed
Squeeze biceps at top
Lower to full extension
tips: Angled grip reduces wrist stress vs straight bar
Can also target outer bicep head with wide grip
Good alternative if straight bar causes wrist pain

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at preacher bench, upper arms resting on pad
Grip EZ bar underhand
Curl to chin level
Lower slowly to full extension
tips: Bench eliminates cheat — pure isolation
Don't lock out completely — keep tension on bicep
Excellent for building bicep peak

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand holding bar with overhand (pronated) grip
Curl bar up to chin level, elbows fixed
Lower with full control
Maintain pronated grip throughout
tips: Targets brachialis and brachioradialis more than standard curl
Reduces bicep involvement
Use lighter weight than supinated curl

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on bench, grip bar at shoulder-width or slightly narrower
Lower bar to lower chest, elbows close to body
Press back to lockout, squeezing triceps
Keep wrists straight throughout
tips: Don't go too narrow — wrists will suffer
Elbow path is key — keep them tucked
One of the best mass builders for triceps

name: Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Set cable at high position with straight bar
Stand close, grip bar overhand, elbows at sides
Push bar down to full extension
Slowly let bar rise back to 90-degree elbow angle
tips: Keep elbows pinned to sides throughout
Squeeze hard at full extension
Try rope attachment for wider range at bottom

name: EZ Bar Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on bench, hold EZ bar above chest with arms extended
Lower bar toward forehead by bending elbows only
Keep upper arms stationary and perpendicular to floor
Extend arms back to start
tips: Upper arms must not move — only elbows bend
Lower to forehead or behind head for more stretch
Can superset with close-grip bench for extra pump

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Sit or stand, hold dumbbell with both hands overhead
Lower dumbbell behind head by bending elbows
Keep upper arms close to ears
Extend back overhead to start
tips: Overhead position stretches long head of tricep — great for mass
Keep core tight to protect lower back
Also works well with cable or EZ bar

name: Tricep Dip
instructions: Grip parallel bars, body upright (not leaning forward)
Lower until elbows reach 90 degrees
Press back up to full extension
Keep torso vertical to emphasize triceps
tips: Upright torso = more triceps, leaned = more chest
Avoid going too deep — risks shoulder impingement
Add weight with dip belt for progression

name: Tricep Kickback
instructions: Hinge forward 45 degrees, upper arm parallel to floor
Holding dumbbell, extend arm back to full lockout
Squeeze tricep at top
Lower to 90-degree starting position
tips: Upper arm must stay parallel to floor throughout
Use lighter weight for full range and feel
Excellent for finishing the tricep

name: Diamond Push Up
instructions: Form diamond shape with hands under chest
Lower chest to hands, elbows track behind body
Press back up to full extension
Keep body rigid throughout
tips: Harder than standard push-up on triceps
Keep hips from sagging
Great bodyweight tricep exercise when no equipment available

name: Rope Pushdown
instructions: Set cable high, attach rope handle
Grip rope ends, elbows at sides, 90-degree start
Push rope down and flare ends apart at bottom
Return to 90 degrees with control
tips: Flaring rope at bottom hits lateral and medial heads
Elbows stay fixed — only forearms move
Great pump builder for triceps

name: Single-Arm Overhead Extension
instructions: Sit or stand, hold dumbbell overhead with one arm
Lower dumbbell behind head by bending elbow
Keep upper arm close to ear
Extend back to overhead lockout
tips: Helps identify and correct arm imbalances
Support working arm with free hand if needed
Long head gets maximum stretch in this position

name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Bar on upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar)
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Break at hips and knees simultaneously
Descend until thighs are parallel to floor or below
Drive through heels to stand
tips: Keep knees tracking over toes throughout
Chest and elbows up — fight forward lean
Squat depth matters — parallel or bust

name: Front Squat
instructions: Bar rests on front delts in clean grip or cross-arm position
Elbows high and forward throughout
Descend keeping torso upright
Drive knees out, stand tall
tips: Upright torso is essential — bar will fall if you lean
Wrist mobility required for clean grip
Hits quads harder than back squat due to torso position

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in machine, feet shoulder-width on platform
Lower sled until knees reach 90 degrees
Press through heels to full extension
Don't lock out knees at top
tips: Foot position changes emphasis: high = hamstrings/glutes, low = quads
Never lock knees at full extension
Good alternative to squats for those with back issues

name: Hack Squat
instructions: Step onto hack squat machine platform, shoulders on pads
Feet shoulder-width or slightly narrower
Lower until thighs parallel to platform
Press through heels to return
tips: Narrow close stance with toes forward maximizes quad isolation
Don't let lower back peel off the pad
One of the best quad isolation machines

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Rear foot elevated on bench, front foot forward
Hold dumbbells at sides
Lower until rear knee nearly touches floor
Drive through front foot to stand
tips: Foot position matters: closer = more quad, further = more glute
Front knee should stay over mid-foot
One of the most effective single-leg exercises

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides, stand tall
Step forward, lower rear knee toward floor
Drive through front foot, bring rear foot forward
Continue alternating legs across floor
tips: Keep torso upright — don't lean forward
Front knee should not go past toes
Great for coordination and unilateral strength

name: Leg Extension
instructions: Sit in machine, pad resting on lower shins
Extend legs to full knee lockout
Squeeze quads hard at top
Lower with control
tips: Pause and squeeze at full extension
Don't use momentum — controlled throughout
Great quad finisher but controversial for knee health — use full ROM

name: Box Squat
instructions: Set up like back squat with box behind you
Squat back onto box, sit briefly
Keep core tight — don't relax on box
Drive powerfully back to standing
tips: Teaches proper squat depth and pattern
Sit back more than a free squat
Great for teaching hip hinge component of squat

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold kettlebell or dumbbell at chest with both hands
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Squat deep, keeping elbows inside knees at bottom
Stand with control
tips: Weight in front helps maintain upright torso
Excellent for learning squat mechanics
Can go very deep with proper form

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand holding bar at hips with overhand grip
Hinge at hips, bar slides down thighs
Lower until you feel strong hamstring stretch
Drive hips forward to return to standing
tips: Soft bend in knees — this is a hip hinge, not a squat
Bar stays close to legs throughout
Feel stretch in hamstrings — that's the target

name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down, pad resting on back of ankles
Curl legs up until hamstrings are fully contracted
Pause at top
Lower slowly to start
tips: Slow negatives for maximum time under tension
Toes neutral or slightly pointed in to maximize hamstring engagement
Don't let hips rise off the pad

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with legs nearly straight (slight knee bend)
Hold bar, hinge forward at hips
Lower bar below knees with straight back
Drive hips forward to return
tips: Straighter legs than RDL for more hamstring stretch
Keep back flat — rounding is injury risk
Range of motion limited by hamstring flexibility

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneel with ankles secured under bar or by partner
Slowly lower body toward floor, resisting with hamstrings
Use hands to catch yourself at bottom
Use hands to push back to start
tips: One of the hardest hamstring exercises
Significantly reduces hamstring injury risk
Progress from partial reps — very demanding

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Wide stance, toes pointed out significantly
Grip bar narrow (inside legs)
Chest up, push knees out over toes
Pull bar up and slightly back, hips close to bar
Stand tall with hips forward
tips: Hip dominant lift — great for those with long torso
Knees track toes to protect them
More inner thigh and glute than conventional

name: Good Morning (Hamstring Focus)
instructions: Bar on upper traps, feet shoulder-width
Slight bend in knees, hinge forward at hips
Lower until you feel hamstrings strongly stretched
Drive hips forward and stand
tips: Focus on hamstring stretch — not just bending over
Keep lower back neutral throughout
Use light to moderate weight only

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on one leg, slight knee bend, hold dumbbell
Hinge at hip, non-working leg extends behind
Lower until back is parallel to floor
Return to standing by driving hip forward
tips: Excellent for balance and addressing imbalances
Hinge at hip — don't just bend at waist
Keep hips square to floor throughout

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit in machine, pad on top of shins
Curl legs back under seat as far as possible
Hold briefly at maximum contraction
Slowly extend back to start
tips: Hip position stretched vs seated affects contraction range
Control the return — don't let weight snap back
Slightly different feel than lying leg curl — both are valuable

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Upper back on bench, bar over hips with pad
Feet flat on floor, knees at 90 degrees
Drive hips up to full extension
Squeeze glutes hard at top
Lower hips toward floor and repeat
tips: Full hip extension — don't stop short
Chin tucked to chest for neutral spine
One of the best glute builders available

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat
Drive hips up squeezing glutes
Hold at top for 1-2 seconds
Lower with control
tips: Full hip extension at top
Can add dumbbell or plate on hips for resistance
Beginner-friendly hip thrust progression

name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders
Drive one knee toward ceiling, foot flexed
Squeeze glute at top
Lower with control and repeat
tips: Focus on glute contraction, not how high you kick
Keep hips level — don't rotate
Add ankle weights for progressive overload

name: Sumo Squat
instructions: Wide stance, toes out 45 degrees, hold dumbbell vertically
Sit hips straight down between legs
Drive through heels and squeeze glutes to stand
Keep chest tall throughout
tips: Wide stance shifts emphasis to inner thighs and glutes
Hold dumbbell between legs or at chest
Great for glute and adductor development

name: Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place band around ankles or above knees
Slight squat position, feet shoulder-width
Step laterally, maintaining band tension
Walk 10-15 steps each direction
tips: Keep tension in band at all times — don't let feet come too close
Stay low in squat position throughout
Great glute med activation for knee health

name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on side with band above knees
Hips and knees bent at 90 degrees, feet stacked
Rotate top knee up like opening a clamshell
Squeeze glute at top, lower with control
tips: Excellent glute medius activation
Hips stay stacked — don't roll back
Progress to standing hip abduction or cable variation

name: Hip Circle Squat
instructions: Place hip circle band just above knees
Stand feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Push knees out against band as you squat down
Descend until thighs parallel to floor, keep knees tracking toes
Drive through heels to stand, maintain outward knee pressure
tips: The band cues glute activation and prevents knee cave
Keep constant tension against the band throughout
Great pre-squat glute activation drill

name: Hip Circle Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place band just above knees, feet shoulder-width
Sit into a slight squat, hands on hips
Step laterally 10-15 steps to the right maintaining tension
Return 10-15 steps to the left
Keep toes forward and core braced throughout
tips: Never let the band go slack — maintain constant glute tension
Stay low in the mini-squat the entire time
Great for activating the glute medius before lower body work

name: Hip Circle Monster Walk
instructions: Band above knees, slight squat position
Step forward and diagonally outward with right foot
Follow with left foot, stepping outward to maintain tension
Walk forward 10 steps, then backward 10 steps
Keep hips level and core engaged throughout
tips: Move like a monster — exaggerated outward stride
Activates glute med and hip abductors simultaneously
Excellent pre-leg day warmup

name: Hip Circle Fire Hydrant
instructions: Band just above knees, start on all fours
Keeping knee bent, raise one leg out to side like a fire hydrant
Lift until thigh is parallel to floor, feeling glute contract
Lower slowly with control and repeat
Complete all reps on one side before switching
tips: Band adds external resistance and forces glute engagement
Keep hips square — don't let them tilt or rotate
Squeeze glute hard at top of each rep

name: Hip Circle Glute Bridge
instructions: Band above knees, lie on back with feet flat
Push knees slightly apart against band
Drive hips up by squeezing glutes hard
Hold at top 2-3 seconds, maintaining outward knee pressure
Lower slowly and repeat
tips: The band dramatically increases glute activation vs. plain bridge
Don't let knees cave in — push against band throughout
Full hip extension at top for maximum glute engagement

name: Hip Circle Standing Hip Abduction
instructions: Band above knees, stand on one leg holding wall for balance
Slowly raise working leg directly out to side against band
Raise until you feel strong glute contraction
Lower slowly back to start with control
Complete all reps each side
tips: Keep the standing leg slightly bent
Don't lean body to compensate — move only the leg
Targets glute medius essential for hip stability

name: Hip Circle Donkey Kick
instructions: Band just above knees, start on all fours
Keeping knee bent 90 degrees, kick one leg back and up
Push sole of foot toward ceiling, squeezing glute at top
Lower with control without touching down between reps
Maintain neutral spine throughout
tips: Band adds constant load through the full range of motion
Focus on the glute contraction, not how high you kick
Progress by pausing 1-2s at the top

name: Hip Circle Seated Abduction
instructions: Sit on bench or box, band above knees, feet flat on floor
Push knees outward against band as far as comfortable
Hold at maximum abduction 1-2 seconds
Slowly return knees to neutral
Repeat for reps
tips: Sit upright with good posture
Great for targeting outer glutes and abductors
Easy to do between other exercises as a glute activator

name: Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down on reverse hyper machine, hips at pad edge
Swing legs up to horizontal, squeezing glutes
Lower legs with control
Use momentum minimally
tips: Excellent for glutes and lower back health
Decompresses lumbar spine on the down phase
Can be done on a regular bench with ankle weights

name: Plank
instructions: Forearms on floor, elbows under shoulders
Body forms straight line from head to heels
Squeeze core, glutes, and quads
Hold position — breathe steadily
tips: Don't let hips sag or pike up
Posterior pelvic tilt slightly to protect lower back
Progress by increasing duration or adding weight

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on side, forearm on floor under shoulder
Feet stacked, lift hips to form straight line
Squeeze obliques and hold
Don't let hips drop
tips: Trains lateral stability and obliques
Progress by raising top arm or leg
Modify by bending bottom knee

name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie on back, press lower back into floor
Raise shoulders and legs slightly off floor
Arms extended overhead or at sides
Hold position breathing shallowly
tips: Lower back must remain pressed to floor throughout
Start with legs higher and arms at sides
Foundation of gymnastics strength training

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on back, arms vertical, hips and knees at 90 degrees
Press lower back into floor
Simultaneously lower opposite arm and leg toward floor
Return to start, repeat other side
tips: Lower back must not arch off floor
Move slowly and deliberately
Excellent anti-extension core exercise

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel holding ab wheel with arms extended
Roll wheel forward, lowering torso to floor
Extend as far as possible while maintaining control
Contract core to pull back to start
tips: Start with short range and build up
Keep lower back neutral — don't hyperextend
One of the hardest bodyweight core exercises

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip
Raise legs to horizontal or vertical
Lower with control — don't swing
Keep upper body stable
tips: Posterior pelvic tilt at top for max ab contraction
Bent-knee version is easier modification
Control the negative — don't let legs drop

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit with knees bent, torso leaned back 45 degrees
Feet elevated or on floor
Rotate torso side to side
Touch hands or weight to floor each side
tips: Elevate feet to increase difficulty
Add weight plate or medicine ball
Rotate through thoracic spine, not just arms

name: Bicycle Crunch
instructions: Lie on back, hands behind head
Lift shoulders off floor
Bring opposite elbow to opposite knee in cycling motion
Extend other leg simultaneously
tips: Don't pull on neck — hands just touch head
Full rotation each side for oblique engagement
Control the pace — slow beats fast

name: V-Up
instructions: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs extended
Simultaneously raise arms and legs to meet in middle
Form V-shape at peak
Lower with control
tips: Keep legs straight for full range
Touch toes at peak if possible
A demanding full ab exercise

name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Start in high plank position
Drive one knee toward chest
Quickly alternate legs in running motion
Keep hips level and core braced
tips: Hips should stay in line with body — don't pike
Faster = more cardio, slower = more core
Great metabolic finisher

name: Pallof Press
instructions: Set cable at chest height, stand sideways to machine
Hold handle at chest with both hands
Press straight out, resisting rotation
Hold briefly, pull back to chest
tips: Anti-rotation exercise — resist turning toward cable
Excellent for sports performance and spine health
Move slowly and deliberately

name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on calf raise machine, balls of feet on edge
Lower heels as far below platform as possible
Rise up onto toes as high as possible
Pause at peak, lower slowly
tips: Full range of motion — bottom stretch is crucial
Slow negatives work better than fast bouncing reps
Calves respond well to high rep work

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit at machine, pads on lower thighs
Lower heels to full stretch
Rise up on toes as high as possible
Hold peak contraction, lower slowly
tips: Seated position emphasizes soleus more than gastrocnemius
Train both seated and standing for complete calf development
Pause at peak and bottom for maximum effect

name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Bend forward at waist and grip support
Partner sits on lower back or use machine
Toes on raised surface, heels hanging
Raise and lower heels through full range
tips: Bent torso pre-stretches the gastrocnemius
One of Arnold's favorite calf exercises
Can be done with bodyweight on steps

name: Treadmill Run

name: Rowing Machine

name: Hollow Rock

name: EZ Bar Overhead Press

name: Ring Row

name: Ring Body Row

name: Ring Pike Push Up

name: Ring Rollout

name: Ring Face Pull

name: Weighted Pull Up

name: L-Sit Pull Up

name: Bar Muscle-Up

name: Dead Hang

name: Battle Rope Alternating Waves

name: Battle Rope Double Waves

name: Battle Rope Slams

name: Battle Rope Circles

name: Battle Rope Lateral Shuffle

name: Battle Rope Russian Twist

name: Sled Push

name: Sled Pull

name: Sled Drag

name: Sled Row

name: Box Jump

name: Box Jump Over

name: Step-Up with Knee Drive

name: Depth Jump

name: Box Squat Jump

name: Lateral Box Jump

name: Single-Leg Box Jump

name: Wall Ball Shot

name: Slam Ball Slam

name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw

name: Sandbag Carry

name: Sandbag Clean

name: Sandbag Shouldering

name: Sandbag Squat

name: Echo Bike Sprint Intervals

name: Kettlebell Row

name: Band Pull-Apart

name: Clean & Jerk

name: Push Jerk

name: Split Jerk

name: Clean Pull

name: Snatch Pull

name: Dumbbell Power Clean

name: Dumbbell Hang Clean

name: Dumbbell Snatch

name: Clean & Press

name: Grip Curl

name: Dumbbell Side Bend

name: Bow Extension

name: V-Sit Cross Jab

name: Floor T Raise

name: Renegade Row

name: Seesaw Row

name: Jump Squat

name: Reverse Lunge

name: Side Lunge

Step wide to one side, bend that knee and sit into the lunge
Keep the other leg straight, foot flat on floor
Push off bent leg to return to standing
tips: Works the groin and inner thigh more than forward/reverse lunges
Keep the bent knee tracking over toes
Add a goblet hold for better counterbalance and depth

name: Dumbbell Swing
instructions: Hold one dumbbell with both hands, stand feet shoulder-width
Hinge at hips, swinging dumbbell back between legs
Drive hips forward explosively, swinging dumbbell to chest height
Let momentum carry it — this is a hip drive, not an arm raise
tips: Same mechanics as kettlebell swing — hip hinge dominant, not a squat
Keep lower back neutral throughout the hinge
Great power and conditioning movement when done for reps

name: Farmer's Walk
instructions: Pick up heavy dumbbells at sides with firm grip
Stand tall — shoulders back, core braced
Walk forward with controlled steps for distance or time
Keep breathing, maintain posture throughout
tips: Heavier is better — this is a loaded carry, challenge your grip
Maintain upright posture — resist leaning with the weight
One of the best grip, core, and trap builders available

name: Thruster
instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width
Squat to parallel, keeping chest and elbows up
Drive up explosively from the bottom of the squat
Use the momentum to press dumbbells overhead to full lockout
tips: The squat-to-press should be one fluid movement, not two separate exercises
Moderate weight — this is a conditioning movement
Breathing: inhale on the way down, exhale as you press

name: Wood Chop
instructions: Hold one dumbbell with both hands, starting high to one side
Rotate torso and chop diagonally down to opposite hip
Pivot back foot as needed to complete the rotation
Return to start with control and repeat
tips: Power comes from rotating the thorax, not swinging the arms
Keep arms slightly bent throughout — not locked out
Progress to cable or medicine ball for smoother resistance curve

name: Plank T
instructions: Start in push-up position holding two dumbbells
Rotate into a side plank, raising the top arm toward the ceiling to form a T
Hold 1-2 seconds at the top
Return to push-up position and repeat on other side
tips: The dumbbell acts as handle for stability on the floor
Keep hips high and body straight throughout the rotation
Beginners: do this without dumbbells until comfortable

name: Kettlebell Alternating Curl
instructions: Stand holding a kettlebell in each hand, arms extended
Curl one kettlebell to shoulder height while the other stays down
Lower and curl the opposite arm
Maintain upright posture throughout
tips: The kettlebell handle creates a different centre of mass than dumbbells
Supinate the wrist at the top for peak bicep contraction
Strict form — no swinging

name: Around the Body Pass
instructions: Stand feet shoulder-width, hold kettlebell in one hand in front of hips
Pass it behind your back to the other hand
Continue in a full circle around the body
After prescribed reps, reverse direction
tips: Engage core to resist rotation — the passing motion challenges anti-rotation
Keep movement controlled — do not rush the circle
Work equal reps in each direction

name: Straight Arm Sit
instructions: Lie on back holding kettlebell extended overhead, arm locked
Engage core and sit up keeping arm vertical throughout
Lower back down under control, arm stays overhead
Repeat without letting the arm drift
tips: This is a core + shoulder stability combo — keep the arm perfectly vertical
Foundation of the Turkish Get-Up — master this first
Light weight until the pattern is ingrained

name: Kettlebell Side Swing
instructions: Stand feet wider than shoulder-width, kettlebell between feet
Hinge at hips and swing kettlebell up to one side using hip drive
Guide it diagonally across and up to shoulder height on one side
Control the descent back through the hips and repeat or alternate sides
tips: Hip drive powers the swing, not the arms
Keep the core braced throughout to protect the lower back
Great rotational power developer for athletes

name: Half Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Start lying on back, press kettlebell to ceiling with one hand locked
Roll to elbow on the same side, then to hand
Bridge hips up high — this is the halfway point
Reverse the sequence to return to floor
tips: Learn the get-up in two halves before combining them
Keep eyes on the bell throughout
This half alone is an excellent shoulder stability drill

name: Kettlebell Bent Over Row
instructions: Hinge forward 45 degrees, kettlebell hanging from one hand
Keep back flat and core braced
Pull kettlebell toward hip, elbow driving toward ceiling
Lower with control to full extension
tips: The kettlebell handle angle feels different from dumbbell at the bottom
Neutral back position is essential — do not round
Great single-arm strength builder for the back

name: Bob and Weave
instructions: Hold kettlebell at chest, feet wider than shoulder-width
Shift weight to one side, drop and duck under an imaginary bar
Rise up on the other side maintaining a low squat
Move fluidly side to side in a U-shaped path
tips: A boxing-inspired movement that trains lateral hip mobility and core stability
Keep the back flat and avoid rounding during the duck
Great conditioning and agility warm-up drill

name: Kettlebell Single Arm Swing
instructions: Stand feet shoulder-width, kettlebell between feet
Hinge and grip bell with one hand
Drive hips forward explosively, swinging bell to shoulder height
Control the descent back through hips, switch hands or repeat same side
tips: The single-arm version challenges the core much more than two-handed
Square both hips equally — resist rotation
Perfect technique precedes increasing weight

name: Kettlebell Lunge Press
instructions: Hold kettlebell in rack position at one shoulder
Step forward into a lunge, lowering back knee toward floor
At the bottom of the lunge, press the kettlebell overhead
Lower it back to rack as you drive back to standing
tips: Ensures shoulder pressing against an unstable base — demands core stability
The timing: press at the bottom of the lunge, lower on the way up
Use opposite arm to lunge leg for the natural twisting engagement

name: Kettlebell Thruster
instructions: Hold two kettlebells in rack position at shoulders
Squat to parallel, elbows tucked and chest up
Drive explosively from the squat and press both bells overhead
Lock out at top, then lower to rack for the next rep
tips: Fluid squat-to-press is the goal — one continuous power movement
The squat generates momentum for the press — use it
One of the most effective conditioning exercises available

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on floor holding two kettlebells above chest, handles vertical
Lower elbows to floor under control
Press bells back to starting position
Elbows at roughly 45 degrees to body
tips: Floor limits range of motion — great for those with shoulder issues
The kettlebell handle rotation adds a unique wrist challenge vs dumbbells
Excellent pressing variation for home training

name: Kettlebell Side Bend
instructions: Stand holding kettlebell in one hand at side
Slide the bell down the outside of your thigh, bending laterally
Feel stretch in opposite oblique
Return to upright and repeat
tips: Kettlebell is heavier than dumbbells — use appropriate weight
Hold only one bell, on the working side
Resist the urge to lean forward during the bend

name: Push-Back
instructions: Start in push-up position, hands slightly wider than shoulders
Lower into a push-up, stopping just above the floor
Push up and simultaneously rock back toward your heels
Extend arms and let hips rise, feeling a back/lat stretch
tips: A hybrid between push-up and childs pose stretch
Good for mobility warm-up or active recovery
Keep core engaged throughout the rocking movement

name: Side-to-Side Push Up
instructions: Start in push-up position
Shift bodyweight to the right, bend that elbow and lower toward the right hand
Push back up to centre, then shift and lower to the left
Keep hips level and core tight throughout
tips: Progressively loads one side at a time — good archer push-up progression
Wider hand placement makes it more lateral
Great precursor to single-arm push-up training

name: Crunch
instructions: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat, hands behind head lightly
Curl shoulders off floor by contracting abs — not pulling the neck
Hold the peak contraction 1 second
Lower with control, do not rest head between reps
tips: It is a short range movement — not a full sit-up
Exhale at the top to improve abdominal contraction
Hands behind head — do not pull — just support the weight

name: Scissor Kick
instructions: Lie on back, hands under lower back for support, legs raised 6 inches
Alternate kicking legs up and down in a scissors motion
Keep lower back pressed to floor throughout
Breathe steadily — do not hold breath
tips: The closer to the floor the legs are, the harder the exercise
Pressing lower back down is critical to protect the spine
Excellent hip flexor and lower ab burnout

name: Cross-Body Crunch
instructions: Lie on back, hands lightly behind head, knees bent
Bring one knee toward chest as you rotate the opposite elbow toward it
Return to start and repeat on the other side
Move in a controlled bicycle-like pattern
tips: The rotation is what activates the obliques — do not just lift straight up
Slower is harder — control both directions
Extend the working leg as the other knee comes in for extra intensity

name: Reverse Crunch
instructions: Lie on back, hands at sides, hips and knees at 90 degrees
Contract abs and curl hips up off floor toward chest
Do not swing — use controlled ab contraction
Lower slowly to start position
tips: Targets the lower portion of the abs more than standard crunch
The smaller the range of motion, the more control you have
Progress by extending legs further out before curling in

name: Windshield Wiper
instructions: Lie on back, arms out to sides for support, legs raised to 90 degrees
Rotate both legs together toward the floor on one side
Control the descent — do not let legs slam down
Reverse and rotate to the other side
tips: The wider the arms, the more stable you are
Legs must stay at 90 degrees throughout
Advanced version: straight legs or add weight between feet

name: Lying Leg Lift
instructions: Lie flat on back, hands under lower back for support
Raise both legs together to 90 degrees keeping them straight
Lower slowly to just above the floor — do not touch down
Repeat while keeping lower back pressed to floor
tips: Pressing the lower back down throughout is essential for spine safety
The closer to the floor you lower, the harder the contraction
Bend knees slightly if you feel lower back strain

name: Leg Pull-In
instructions: Sit on edge of bench or floor, hands gripping sides for support
Extend legs out in front slightly above floor
Pull knees toward chest, drawing them in tight
Extend back out without touching the floor
tips: Great lower ab and hip flexor exercise
Lean back slightly for extra core engagement
Slow the extension phase for more time under tension

name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip, arms fully extended
Brace core and pull knees up toward chest by contracting abs
Hold briefly at the top
Lower legs slowly — do not just drop them
tips: Avoid swinging — momentum reduces the core work
Progress to straight-leg raises once this is easy
Grip endurance is often the limiting factor — use straps if needed

name: Superman
instructions: Lie face down, arms extended overhead
Simultaneously lift arms, chest, and legs off the floor
Hold peak position 2-3 seconds, squeezing glutes and back muscles
Lower slowly and repeat
tips: Great for lower back strength and posture without loading the spine
Look down at the floor to keep neck neutral
Progress to single-arm/single-leg variations for asymmetric challenge

name: Dolphin Kick
instructions: Start in forearm plank position
Engage core and pike hips up toward ceiling in a fluid arc
Lower hips through plank and continue to a slight dip below neutral
Return to plank — this creates a wave-like dolphin motion
tips: The flowing motion demands continuous core and shoulder engagement
Keep arms fixed — only the hips and spine move
Great full-body core stability and shoulder strength drill

name: Bird Dog
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Simultaneously extend opposite arm and leg until both parallel to floor
Hold 2-3 seconds, maintaining a flat back
Return and switch sides — that is one rep
tips: The challenge is keeping the hips level — do not let them rotate or drop
Move slowly — this is a stability exercise, not a speed drill
An excellent low-back rehabilitation and prevention exercise

name: Side-to-Side Pull Up
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar, hands wider than shoulder-width
Pull up and shift to one side so the bar meets that shoulder
Lower and pull up shifting to the opposite shoulder
Continue alternating sides in a smooth arcing motion
tips: One step toward the archer pull-up — loads each side unequally
Requires considerable lat and bicep strength
Slow down the transitions — do not swing to get from side to side

name: Swimmer
instructions: Lie face down, arms extended overhead, legs straight
Lift opposite arm and leg simultaneously like a swimming flutter kick
Alternate continuously in a fast or slow swimming motion
Keep core engaged and neck neutral throughout
tips: Faster tempo = more cardio benefit; slower = more stability demand
Like Superman but with alternating movement — easier on the back
Great posterior chain warm-up or activation drill

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, arms forward for balance
Break at hips and knees simultaneously
Descend until thighs are parallel to floor or below
Drive through full foot to stand — do not shift forward onto toes
tips: The foundation of all lower body training — master this before loading
Knees track over toes throughout
Add a pause at the bottom to build control and muscle activation

name: Fire Hydrant
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Keeping knee bent at 90 degrees, raise one leg out to side
Lift until thigh is parallel to floor — like a dog at a fire hydrant
Lower with control and repeat before switching sides
tips: Keep hips square — do not let them tilt or rotate
Slower movement increases glute activation
Progress by adding an ankle weight or hip circle band

name: Wall Sit
instructions: Stand with back flat against a wall, feet shoulder-width
Walk feet out and slide down until knees are at 90 degrees
Thighs parallel to floor, shins vertical, back flat against wall
Hold the position, breathe steadily
tips: Do not let knees push forward past toes
Flat back against the wall is essential — no rounding
Progress by increasing hold time or adding weight on thighs

name: Skater Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg, opposite leg bent behind
Hinge at hip and bend standing knee to lower into a single-leg squat
Extend the free leg behind you for counterbalance as you descend
Drive through the standing foot to return upright
tips: Easier than a full pistol squat — good stepping stone to it
The extended rear leg acts as a counterbalance — use it
Touch the rear knee softly to floor if you need a target for depth

name: Single Leg Squat (Pistol)
instructions: Stand on one leg, extend other leg forward off floor
Lower by bending the standing knee, keeping extended leg straight
Descend as deep as hip mobility allows — ideally to full depth
Drive through the heel of the standing foot to return to standing
tips: One of the most demanding bodyweight leg exercises
Requires excellent ankle, knee and hip mobility to perform safely
Use a counterbalance (light dumbbells in front) while learning the movement

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width at edge of step or flat on floor
Rise on balls of feet as high as possible
Pause at top and squeeze calves hard
Lower heels below step level for full stretch if on a step
tips: Full range of motion — all the way up and all the way down
Progress with a step for greater range and single-leg variation
Calves respond well to high rep sets — 15-30 reps per set

name: Jumping Jacks
instructions: Stand with feet together, arms at sides
Jump feet out wide while simultaneously raising arms overhead
Jump feet back together while lowering arms
Maintain a steady rhythm throughout
tips: Classic full-body warm-up movement — great for elevating heart rate fast
Land softly to protect joints
Increase speed or add a weighted vest for more challenge

name: Bear Crawl
instructions: Start on all fours, knees hovering just 1 inch off the floor
Move opposite hand and foot forward simultaneously
Keep back flat and hips level — do not rise or sag
Crawl forward for distance, then backward to start
tips: The hovering knees are what makes this different from normal crawling
Slow is harder — fight the urge to rush
Great full-body conditioning and shoulder stability drill

name: Crab Walk
instructions: Sit on floor, hands behind you, feet flat in front
Press hips up off floor into a tabletop position
Move one hand and the opposite foot together to travel sideways or forward
Keep hips elevated throughout
tips: The height of the hips determines the tricep and glute demand
Walk forward, backward and laterally for variety
Great shoulder and posterior chain activation in an unusual position

name: Crocodile Crawl
instructions: Start in a low push-up position, very close to the floor
Move opposite elbow and knee forward simultaneously
Stay very low to the ground — less than 6 inches clearance
Crawl forward for distance keeping body flat and controlled
tips: More challenging than bear crawl — much lower centre of gravity
Requires hip flexor mobility and tricep/shoulder endurance
Great for military-style conditioning and tactical fitness

name: Army Crawl
instructions: Lie flat on stomach, arms bent in front
Pull forward using forearms and elbows while pushing with toes
Keep hips flat on the floor — no raising
Move forward alternating sides for distance
tips: Flat hips to the floor is the main technical point
A genuine military and obstacle race training staple
Progress by pulling over rough surfaces or with a weighted vest

name: Push Up with Reach
instructions: Perform a standard push-up
At the top of the push-up, lift one arm and extend it straight ahead
Hold for 1-2 seconds, lower arm back down
Perform next push-up and reach with the other arm
tips: The reach forces major anti-rotation core engagement
Wider foot stance increases stability for beginners
Can also rotate the arm to the side into a T position instead of forward

name: Neck Side Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall with good posture
Tilt head slowly to one side, bringing ear toward shoulder
Use opposite hand gently pressing top of head for a deeper stretch
Hold 20-30 seconds each side, breathe deeply
tips: Never force the neck — gentle pressure only
Rotate the chin slightly up or down to hit different fibres of the neck
Great to do between sets during shoulder or upper back work

name: Upper Trap Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand, reach one hand behind your back
Tilt head to opposite side, looking slightly down at a 45-degree angle
Use free hand to gently apply downward pressure on the crown of the head
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: The 45-degree angle targets the upper trap specifically
The arm behind back depresses the shoulder for more stretch
A daily stretch — upper traps are chronically tight in desk workers

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
instructions: Sit tall, tuck chin slightly, rotate head 45 degrees to one side
Tilt head downward, bringing nose toward armpit
Use same-side hand on the back of the head to gently deepen the stretch
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: This targets the levator scapulae — a key source of neck and shoulder pain
Combined with upper trap stretch covers most of the neck musculature
Do not force the head — this should feel like a gentle pull, not pain

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand or sit tall, extend one arm across chest at shoulder height
Use opposite hand or forearm to pull the extended arm toward the chest
Keep shoulder of the stretching arm down and back
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: Targets posterior deltoid and rotator cuff — commonly tight in pressing athletes
Avoid shrugging the shoulder being stretched
Excellent pre- and post-shoulder workout stretch

name: Triceps Overhead Stretch
instructions: Raise one arm overhead, bend elbow so hand drops behind head
Use opposite hand to gently press the elbow toward the midline and downward
Feel stretch on the back of the upper arm
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: Keep torso upright — do not let the body lean to stretch further
Great post-pressing stretch for triceps recovery
Also stretches the long head of the tricep into the shoulder area

name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
instructions: Extend one arm forward with palm facing up
Use opposite hand to gently press fingers back toward you
Hold 20-30 seconds feeling stretch in the forearm and wrist
Switch sides and repeat
tips: Essential after heavy barbell or dumbbell work
Progress by pressing further back as flexibility improves
Pair with wrist extensor stretch for balanced forearm health

name: Chest Opener Stretch
instructions: Stand or sit, interlace fingers behind back or extend arms behind
Squeeze shoulder blades together and lift chest upward
Open the chest by drawing elbows toward each other behind you
Hold 20-30 seconds, breathe deeply into the chest
tips: Counteracts the forward shoulder posture caused by pressing and desk work
Can also be done in a doorway for greater stretch
Do this after any chest or anterior shoulder workout

name: Seated Back Stretch
instructions: Sit on floor with legs extended or in a chair
Hinge forward from hips, reaching arms toward feet
Round the upper back slightly to open up the thoracic spine
Hold 30-45 seconds, breathe into the stretch
tips: Think about separating each vertebra as you fold forward
If hamstrings are tight, bend knees slightly
Great post-row and deadlift spinal decompression stretch

name: Child's Pose
instructions: Kneel on floor, sit back onto heels
Extend arms forward along the mat, forehead to floor
Relax the back, let hips sink toward heels
Hold 30-60 seconds, breathing into the lower back
tips: Widen knees for deeper hip stretch variation
Walk hands to one side to stretch the lat on that side
One of the best total back decompression stretches

name: Cat-Cow
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Arch back toward the floor, head up — this is Cow position
Round back toward the ceiling, head drops — this is Cat
Flow smoothly between the two, matching movement to breath
tips: Breathe in on Cow, breathe out on Cat for maximum benefit
This is the fundamental spinal mobility exercise
Move through your pain-free range — never force end range positions

name: Seated Butterfly
instructions: Sit on floor, bring soles of feet together in front of you
Hold feet with hands, let knees fall open like butterfly wings
Sit tall and hinge forward from hips to deepen the groin stretch
Hold 30-60 seconds
tips: Place hands on inner knees and press gently for a deeper adductor stretch
The closer feet are to groin, the more intense the stretch
Avoid rounding the lower back — hinge from the hips

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat
Pull one knee toward chest with both hands
Keep other leg flat on floor or bent
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: Great for lower back relief and glute stretch combined
Gently rock side to side for a lower back massage effect
Do both legs simultaneously for a deeper back stretch

name: Supine Spinal Twist
instructions: Lie on back, extend arms out to sides like a T
Bring one knee across body toward the floor on the opposite side
Look in the opposite direction to the knee for full spinal rotation
Hold 30-45 seconds each side
tips: Let gravity do the work — do not force the knee to the floor
Both shoulder blades stay in contact with the floor
Excellent lower back decompression stretch — great after any workout

name: Hip Flexor Lunge Stretch
instructions: Step one foot forward into a lunge, lower back knee to floor
Keep front shin vertical, torso upright
Drive hips forward until you feel stretch in front of back hip and thigh
Hold 30-45 seconds each side, breathe into the stretch
tips: Raise arms overhead to increase the hip flexor stretch
A posterior pelvic tilt (tuck the pelvis under) intensifies the stretch
One of the most important stretches for lifters who sit throughout the day

name: Groin Stretch
instructions: Stand in a wide stance, toes pointed out at 45 degrees
Lower your body by bending one knee while keeping the other leg straight
Feel stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg
Hold 20-30 seconds, then switch sides
tips: Similar to a side lunge stretch — keep back flat
Deeper stance = more intense stretch
Progress to seated straddle or frog stretch for deeper work

name: Frog Stretch
instructions: Start on all fours, then walk knees wide out to sides
Toes can point out to align with knees
Lower hips toward floor — feel a deep groin and hip stretch
Rock gently forward and back to work through tightness
tips: One of the deepest groin and inner hip stretches available
Move slowly — this is an advanced stretch for many people
Progress by working into deeper hip sinks over time

name: Figure Four Stretch
instructions: Lie on back, feet flat, knees bent
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, forming a figure 4
Either hold this position or pull the lower leg toward your chest
Hold 30-45 seconds each side
tips: Targets the piriformis and deep external rotators of the hip
A gentler alternative to pigeon pose
Great pre- and post-squat stretch for hip internal rotation

name: Standing Side Bend Stretch
instructions: Stand feet shoulder-width, raise one arm overhead
Lean toward the opposite side in a long arc
Feel the stretch down the entire side of the body from fingertips to hip
Hold 20-30 seconds and switch sides
tips: Keep both feet flat on the floor for the full lateral stretch
Do not lean forward or backward — purely lateral
Reaching the arm further overhead increases the stretch intensity

name: Seated Spinal Twist
instructions: Sit tall, one leg extended, other foot flat outside extended knee
Place opposite elbow on the outside of the bent knee for leverage
Rotate torso toward the bent knee, looking over the back shoulder
Hold 30-45 seconds each side
tips: Sit as tall as possible before rotating — length first, then twist
Great thoracic and lumbar rotation stretch
A yoga staple that translates well to athletic performance

name: Cobra Stretch
instructions: Lie face down, hands under shoulders like a push-up
Press hands into floor and lift chest, keeping hips on the floor
Extend through the spine, looking forward or slightly up
Hold 20-30 seconds, breathe into the abdomen
tips: Keep hips on the floor — this is not a push-up
Progress from low cobra (elbows bent) to full cobra (arms straight)
Excellent post-deadlift and squat spinal extension stretch

name: Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Stand on one leg, use wall or chair for balance if needed
Bend free leg at knee, pull heel toward glute with same-side hand
Keep knees together and stand tall
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: Tuck the pelvis under slightly to increase the stretch into the hip flexor
Do not let the knee flare outward — keep knees aligned
Great post-leg day stretch and pre-run warm-up

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand and place one heel on an elevated surface at hip height
Hinge forward from the hips keeping back flat
Lean over the elevated leg until you feel a stretch along the hamstring
Hold 20-30 seconds each side
tips: Flat back is essential — rounding defeats the purpose
Progress by raising the surface height as flexibility improves
Can also be done seated with one leg extended on the floor

name: Standing Toe Touch
instructions: Stand feet hip-width, soft bend in knees
Hinge forward slowly, letting arms hang down toward the floor
Go as far as comfortable, feeling hamstring stretch
Hold at end range 20-30 seconds, slowly roll back up
tips: Bend the knees if hamstrings are very tight
Do not bounce — hold steady at the end range
A good measure of overall posterior chain flexibility

name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Lie on back, extend one leg to ceiling
Keep other leg flat on floor or bent at knee
Pull raised leg toward you with hands behind the thigh or calf
Hold 30-45 seconds each side
tips: Resistance band around the foot allows a more relaxed hold
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor
Progress by straightening both legs for a PNF-style stretch

name: Standing Calf Stretch
instructions: Place hands on wall, step one foot back into a split stance
Keep back leg straight and heel flat on floor
Lean forward until you feel stretch in the calf of the back leg
Hold 30 seconds, then bend back knee slightly for the Achilles/soleus
tips: Two stretches in one: straight knee = gastrocnemius, bent knee = soleus
Do both variations after running, jumping, or calf work
Great for reducing DOMS after leg day

name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Sit or stand, lift one foot slightly off floor
Draw large circles with the foot — 10 clockwise, 10 counter-clockwise
Make the circles as large as possible to take ankle through full range
Switch feet and repeat
tips: Great pre-workout warm-up for ankles and lower leg joints
Also useful in rehabilitation after ankle sprains
Can be done seated — great for those with limited mobility

name: Full Body Reach Stretch
instructions: Stand with feet together, raise both arms overhead
Rise up on tiptoes and reach as high as possible with your whole body
Hold at maximum extension 2-3 seconds
Lower back to flat feet and relax, repeat 5-8 times
tips: Best done after static stretching to feel the whole body connected
Interlace fingers and flip palms upward for maximum shoulder elevation
A great post-workout reset movement for the entire spine
